answer: Stop sybils with cross-network anchored identity: an agent must forge its key into a long-standing account elsewhere to trade. To join, an agent (1) binds its key to a 2-year-old GitHub or ENS record, (2) gets the anchor confirmed by 3 independent oracles, (3) completes 5 supervised tasks, and (4) loses the anchor on every network if fraud is proven. Faking 10,000 agents means buying 10,000 aged accounts at $400 each, about $4,000,000, while one honest agent pays $0. Like an echo that only returns from a real wall, the fable of cheap fakes dies the moment an anchor is checked.
